privacy.ai_training_note: Default is Learning Mode: customer translations are stored and used to improve Lara's translation model in real-time ('Every approved translation feeds back into Lara'). Incognito Mode is available (no storage). Lara T&C Section 4.2 grants permission 'for refining the translation model.' However, Google Sheets integration explicitly promises no training use; this same guarantee is absent from API/translation-memory documentation. Third-party analysis (Loekalization, June 2026) documents contradictions between support responses and binding terms. The 25M-translation training dataset is sourced from professional translations plus Matecat (a free tool where the default is public visibility unless users apply a privacy key), creating potential consent gaps for confidential material. Enterprise/paid tiers can negotiate zero-storage contracts.

flags: Lara's own documentation contains conflicting statements. Help center claims translations improve 'the translation model' (shared); DPA claims only update 'Translation Memories' (private); developer docs claim 'no model training required.' Binding T&C Section 4.2 permits 'refining the translation model.' Google Sheets integration explicitly excludes training use, but the same promise is absent from API/translation-memory docs. Third-party analysis (Loekalization, June 2026) documented these gaps with no vendor response for a week.
Customer data is stored and used for model improvement by default. Incognito Mode (no storage) is opt-in, not the default. This is a design choice that may not align with privacy-first expectations.

The 25M-translation training dataset includes segments from Matecat (free tool), where the default is public visibility unless users actively apply a privacy key. This raises potential consent issues for confidential client-owned material.

Only SOC 2 Type 1 is held, not Type 2 (no extended control-period audit). Suitable for operational assurance but not ideal for detailed controls testing or organizations requiring longer audit trails.
Not suitable for healthcare (HIPAA), government (FedRAMP), or strict privacy-extension (ISO 27701) requirements. No evidence of ISO 27018 (cloud privacy).
Marketing emphasizes 'secure translation workflow' and 'data protected from start to finish,' but default Learning Mode enables shared-model training without explicit per-project consent disclosure.
Primary data center in EU/EEA, but Amazon infrastructure can process in 'EU or USA'; this geographic flexibility introduces residency uncertainty for strict EU-only requirements.
